test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 15 March, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'** i.e.** ''Send'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **In the given passage,** it is **mentioned that** glutamate is a chemical normally used to (blank number 4) signals from nerve cells.
 
• **Glutamate** is an important neurotransmitter involved in the transmission of signals between nerve cells in the brain.
 
• **Option 3) "send"** is the correct answer because it accurately represents the action of glutamate in sending or transmitting signals from nerve cells.
 
• **Glutamate acts** as an excitatory neurotransmitter, facilitating the communication between neurons.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *Normally used to **send **signals from nerve cells, in large quantities glutamate alters the **performance** of a brain region involved in planning and decision making, the lateral prefrontal cortex (lPFC).*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1) "swipe"** does not accurately describe the action of glutamate in transmitting signals. "Swipe" is typically associated with physical motions and does not fit in the context of neurotransmission.
 
• **Option 2) "donate"** does not align with the function of glutamate in the nervous system. "Donate" means giving or contributing, which is unrelated to the transmission of signals between nerve cells.
 
• **Option 4) "travel"** is not the appropriate term to describe the action of glutamate in signal transmission. While signals do travel in the brain, the specific role of glutamate is to transmit or send those signals.
